findings.where: First screen, the lede under Mark's line ('I advise multilateral development banks, development agencies and governments…'), and the whole page below it
findings.fault: The page says who Mark advises but never shows it. No body that asked him for work is named, and there is no role, region, year or credential anywhere on the page. The only proof of standing is a lecture title with a date. Next to the one action, a visitor has nothing they could check.
findings.who_objects: A development bank's procurement or task-team officer arriving from LinkedIn. They pick people against terms of reference by relevant work and region, so 'I advise multilateral development banks' is a claim they cannot check. They have to leave the page to find out whether he has done work like theirs before writing.

findings.where: Whole page: first screen, lede, footer
findings.fault: Nothing says where Mark works: no base country and no regions of his work. The heading and lede talk about PPPs and governments in general, so the 5-second test leaves 'where' unanswered.
findings.who_objects: An agency officer looking for someone for a project in a given region. Their first filter is whether this advisor has worked in a region like theirs, and the page gives no sign.

findings.where: First screen, the hero photograph's caption ('Placeholder: Mark's photo from the current site, until the image round.') compared with the article image's caption ('An interview at the Belt and Road summit. Placeholder: …')
findings.fault: The hero shows Mark speaking at a lectern, but its caption gives only the placeholder note and never names the event. The article's caption does name its event. So the one image with real weight reads as a portrait, not as a talk at a named event.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor sizing up his standing. A named conference stage is checkable proof that he is asked to speak, but unnamed, it is just a photo of a man at a microphone.

findings.where: The article specimen, the lecture row ('Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the 'Abundance' Challenge · Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF')
findings.fault: His newest talk gives a date but not where or for whom it was given, so the one piece of recent work on the page loses its standing.
findings.who_objects: A procurement reader. 'Who asked him' is the signal they weigh, so a lecture with no host or venue tells them only that he wrote something.

findings.where: First screen, the heading 'In my view, we are at a turning point in the story of Public-Private Partnerships.'
findings.fault: The heading promises an argument (what turning point, and why now), but nothing on the page picks it up or links to where he makes it. A visitor gets a claim with no payoff, and the article below is about something else (what a PPP law should contain).
findings.who_objects: A visitor who reads the big line first and wants to know what Mark thinks the turning point is. With no answer or link they are left with a slogan, which works against the 'real advisor, real judgement' impression the heading is meant to give.

findings.where: Top navigation (Profile · Articles and talks · Blog), desktop and phone
findings.fault: The navigation has no 'Contact' item. Once a visitor scrolls past the hero, the only way to reach Mark is the address in the footer.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who reads on, or who arrives on an article from a shared link, and then decides to get in touch. They look for Contact in the navigation as on every advisor's site, don't find it, and have to hunt for the footer.
